title: The box behind the counter
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The fireworks arrive: a box behind the counter, the catalog's garish drawn as a plain cardboard cube with a warning as blocks. The uncle won't let anyone open it till the third. Gully sits on it. That's allowed.

panels.composition: The shack. A cardboard box behind the counter, a printed warning on its side as blocks. The UNCLE in the chair, through the door. GULLY sitting on the box. WOOD, BARNABY.

image.prompt: a teenager sitting on a cardboard box behind a bait shack counter, an old man visible through the door in a lawn chair, a young man and a dog, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The box. The warning. A hand — the uncle's? no, Gully's — resting on it.

image.prompt: close on a cardboard box with a printed warning label and a young hand resting on top, black and white, no words
an old man in a lawn chair speaking through a doorway without turning, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The shack from the launch. The chair. The box inside, a shape. The dog asleep against it. Everything waiting for the third.
